name: Luzon Striped-Babbler
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (northern luzon)
description: A fairly small bird of lowland and foothill forest and overgrown disturbed areas on Luzon. Rufous-brown on the wings, back, and tail, with a gray head, heavily-streaked pale underparts, and a black face and moustache stripe.

name: Streak-capped Antwren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southeastern bahia) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Tiny hyperactive antwren of the canopy in humid forest and second growth, where it often follows mixed-species flocks. Males are heavily streaked on the head and flanks with a rufous back, dark wings with pale yellowish underparts below.

name: Pale-winged Trumpeter
rangeDescription: Eastern peru to central brazil and northeastern bolivia
description: Unmistakable bird of mature lowland rainforest. Spherical black body with bold white wing patch perched on long legs, yellow bill.

name: Ground Woodpecker
rangeDescription: South africa and lesotho
description: A large, sociable, ground-loving woodpecker of open, lightly-vegetated country, where it prefers to perch on rocks. It has grayish olive upperparts, pale eyes, and a pink washed breast.

name: Schneider's Pitta
rangeDescription: Primary forest of montane sumatra
description: Large-headed and long-legged, this rare and rotund Sumatran endemic is found only in foothill forests between 900 to 2400 meters (typically in the upper half), where it is most easily detected by its strange song, a spaceship-like “oowOOOOwooWOOH.” Male has a sky-blue back and incomplete black collar, while the female has a dull brownish back and a dull blue tail. Both sexes have a rich cinnamon crown and nape, as well as a dark line extending behind the eye.

name: Reunion White-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of réunion (western mascarene islands)
description: An unusual white-eye with dark plumage and a long, curved bill. Olive-green above and gray below with a broad white eye-ring.

name: Scaly Weaver
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola, namibia, far southern zambia, botswana, zimbabwe, and northern and central south africa
description: A very small, sandy-colored finch-like weaver with a scaly crown, a pale pink bill, and a black moustache on a white throat that gives it a fierce-looking expression. Small groups are resident and nomadic in grassy arid savanna, where there are trees and scrub nearby in which to build their untidy oval grass nests.

name: Philippine Hawk-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Philippines
description: A fairly large bird of lowland and montane forest. Dark gray-brown above with a rather long barred tail, a rufous chest, a gray hood, and a white throat.

name: Adelie Penguin
rangeDescription: Circumpolar antarctic seas to edge of ice pack
description: The “classic” penguin, black above and white below. Also note stubby reddish bill and white eyering.

name: Yellow-bellied Sunbird-Asity
rangeDescription: Rainforest of east-central madagascar
description: Tiny, round, short-tailed yellow-bellied bird with a thin curved bill. Males are blue on the back and have bright bare skin around the eye in breeding plumage.

name: Dwarf Honeyguide
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern democratic republic of the congo, western rwanda, western burundi, and southwestern uganda
description: Small and nondescript honeyguide. Note the short but chunky bill and the white patches on the sides of the tail.

name: Wilkins's Finch
rangeDescription: Nightingale island (south atlantic ocean)
description: A chunky olive-yellow finch with a hefty grosbeak-like bill. Male typically has a paler base to the bill and female is smaller, duller, and streakier.

name: Atoll Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Larger islands in tuamotu archipelago (except makatea)
description: A colorful dove, mostly green with a yellow belly, green wings, a silver neck and chest, and in the male, a limited magenta forehead patch. Similar to Makatea Fruit-Dove, but with much more washed-out coloring and pink instead of dark legs.

name: Black Rosy-Finch
rangeDescription: Mountains of idaho and montana to nevada and utah; winters to arizona
description: The darkest of the three rosy-finches with a dark chocolate body. Look for pink highlights in the wings and tail; gray wraps around the back of head.

name: Puerto Rican Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Varied wooded habitats on puerto rico including isla de vieques (just east of puerto rico)
description: A medium-sized woodpecker that frequently forms small flocks and can be found in most wooded habitats. No other species in its range sports its glossy dark blue back and rosy front.

name: Subdesert Mesite
rangeDescription: Coastal subdesert of southwestern madagascar
description: Odd ground-dwelling bird that is rarely seen by those not looking for it. Males have pale underparts with dark spots, while females have heavy reddish markings below.

name: Gray-headed Oliveback
rangeDescription: Guinea-bissau and guinea eastward to central african republic, southwestern south sudan, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and western uganda
description: A large, spectacular, distinctive olive-and-grayish waxbill with a white face and cheeks and a striking black bib that recurves under the cheeks as a jaw-stripe. Juvenile is duller and darker than adult.

name: Restless Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Northern queensland to victoria and southern south australia; southwestern western australia
description: A sturdy songbird with fairly long tail and substantial bill. Glossy black above, bright white below.

name: Whiskered Pitta
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern luzon (northern philippines)
description: A medium-sized bird of lower-elevation montane forest floor and undergrowth on Luzon. Prefers thick undergrowth with moss, ferns, and a steep slope.

name: Southern White-faced Owl
rangeDescription: Southeastern gabon, southern democratic republic of the congo, southern uganda, and southwestern kenya southward to namibia, northern and central south africa, lesotho, eswatini, and mozambique
description: A large scops-owl, but still small relative to large owls. Gray on the back; pale and streaked below with a contrasting black-and-white face.
